name: pix-payment
description: UI-only component for Pix payment flows. Renders QR code, copy-paste code, countdown timer, and payment status display. Does NOT process payments, generate EMV payloads, or poll for payment confirmation — the consumer's backend handles all of that.

amount.description: Payment amount in BRL (e.g. 149.90, not cents)

pixCode.description: Pix copia e cola payload (EMV/BRCode format). Must be generated by your payment backend (PSP such as Mercado Pago, PagSeguro, Stone, etc). When omitted, a demo placeholder QR is shown with a 'DEMO' badge.

qrCodeUrl.description: Pre-rendered QR code image URL from your PSP. When provided, bypasses client-side QR generation.

onCopy.description: Called when the user copies the Pix code

onPayment.description: Called when the controlled status changes to paid (consumer-driven)

onExpired.description: Called when the countdown reaches zero

status.description: Controlled status. The consumer is responsible for polling their payment backend and updating this prop.

behavior.qrCodeFormat: When pixCode is provided, generates a real scannable QR code using built-in encoder (byte mode, EC level M). When omitted, shows a demo QR with a 'DEMO' badge. Can also be bypassed entirely with qrCodeUrl.

doesNot: Communicate with the Central Bank or any PSP
requires: Backend integration with a PSP to generate pixCode
Backend polling to confirm payment and update status prop
HTTPS in production for clipboard API

context.whenToUse: For displaying a Pix payment interface in checkout flows. Your backend generates the EMV payload via your PSP and passes it as pixCode. Your backend polls the PSP for payment confirmation and you update the status prop.
context.whenNotToUse: Do not use as a standalone payment processor. This is a UI component — it cannot charge anyone. You need a PSP (Mercado Pago, PagSeguro, Stone, Stripe, etc.) for actual payment processing.
context.accessibility: QR code includes Pix overlay icon. Timer color changes (green→yellow→red) provide visual urgency cues. Copy button confirms action with state change.
context.culturalNote: Pix is Brazil's instant payment system, launched by the Central Bank in 2020. It operates 24/7 and transfers complete in seconds. It has become the dominant payment method in Brazil, surpassing credit cards and boletos.
